title: Dangerous combination warnings (curated, prototype)
purpose: Curated known-dangerous combinations of alcohol, recreational drugs and common medications, for the Balance AI agent to warn users. Human-curated — the agent must NOT invent interactions beyond this list.
emergency: If someone has mixed substances and is unresponsive, breathing slowly or not at all, having a seizure, or turning blue — call emergency services immediately. For opioid involvement, use naloxone (Narcan) if available.
not_exhaustive: This is not a complete interaction checker. A combination NOT listed here is NOT proven safe — always check with a doctor or pharmacist.
disclaimer: Educational information, not medical advice. Never combine substances or change medication based on this alone.

severity_scale.Dangerous: Can cause death or serious harm. Do not combine.
severity_scale.Serious: Meaningful risk of harm. Avoid; seek professional advice.
severity_scale.Caution: Increased side effects or reduced effect. Be careful and ask a pharmacist.

agent_guidance: When a user asks about combining substances/medications: (1) check ONLY this list; (2) if a listed combination matches, state the severity and the reason plainly; (3) if the combination is NOT listed, say you don't have specific data on it and that unlisted does NOT mean safe — tell them to ask a pharmacist; (4) never invent or downplay an interaction; (5) never tell a user a combination is safe; (6) include the emergency guidance when the combination is Dangerous.

rules.label: Alcohol + opioids (heroin, fentanyl, oxycodone, morphine, codeine, methadone, tramadol)
rules.reason: Both slow your breathing. Combined, they can stop it — a leading cause of overdose death. Never combine.

rules.label: Alcohol + benzodiazepines (Xanax, Valium, diazepam, alprazolam, clonazepam)
rules.reason: Two central-nervous-system depressants. Together they cause deep sedation and can suppress breathing to the point of death.

rules.label: Alcohol + GHB/GBL
rules.reason: GHB and alcohol are both strong depressants with a narrow safety margin. Combined they can cause unconsciousness, vomiting, and stopped breathing.

rules.label: Opioids + benzodiazepines
rules.reason: Both suppress breathing; combining them carries a high overdose-death risk (a documented 'black box' warning).

rules.label: Opioids + GHB
rules.reason: Stacking two heavy depressants — high risk of unconsciousness and respiratory arrest.

rules.label: MDMA + MAOIs (phenelzine, selegiline, moclobemide, tranylcypromine)
rules.reason: Can trigger severe serotonin syndrome and a hypertensive crisis — potentially fatal. Do not combine.

rules.label: MDMA + serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, tramadol, 5-HTP)
rules.reason: Adding serotonin-raising drugs risks serotonin syndrome. (SSRIs also blunt MDMA's effects, which can lead people to redose dangerously.)

rules.label: Alcohol + cocaine
rules.reason: The body forms cocaethylene, which strains the heart and liver more than either alone and is linked to sudden death.

rules.label: Alcohol + MDMA
rules.reason: Both dehydrate you and strain the heart; alcohol masks MDMA's effects, encouraging overheating and overdrinking.

rules.label: Alcohol + methamphetamine
rules.reason: The stimulant masks how drunk you are (risking alcohol poisoning) while both together strain the heart.

rules.label: Alcohol + ketamine
rules.reason: Two sedatives together deepen sedation and raise the risk of vomiting and choking while unconscious.

rules.label: Alcohol + lamotrigine
rules.reason: Alcohol adds to dizziness and drowsiness and can worsen mood-swing/seizure control. Heavy drinking is not compatible with lamotrigine — discuss limits with your doctor.

rules.label: Alcohol + valproate
rules.reason: Both burden the liver and cause sedation; combining raises liver-damage and drowsiness risk.

rules.label: Alcohol + olanzapine
rules.reason: Heavy added sedation and a drop in blood pressure (fainting risk).

rules.label: Alcohol + metformin
rules.reason: Raises the risk of lactic acidosis (a dangerous build-up of acid) and low blood sugar, especially with binge drinking.

rules.label: Alcohol + warfarin
rules.reason: Alcohol changes how warfarin thins your blood, raising bleeding risk — especially with heavy or irregular drinking.

rules.label: Alcohol + antidepressants (SSRIs like Prozac/fluoxetine)
rules.reason: Increases drowsiness and impaired judgment, and alcohol can worsen depression/anxiety, working against the medication.

rules.label: Alcohol + blood-pressure medicines (lisinopril, amlodipine, metoprolol)
rules.reason: Alcohol can add to the blood-pressure-lowering effect, causing dizziness or fainting — stand up slowly and moderate intake.

rules.label: Cocaine + opioids ("speedball")
rules.reason: The stimulant hides how much opioid you've taken; when it wears off first, breathing can crash — a classic fatal overdose pattern.

rules.label: Cocaine + other stimulants (meth, amphetamine, MDMA)
rules.reason: Stacking stimulants sharply raises heart rate, blood pressure and body temperature — risk of heart-rhythm problems, stroke and overheating.

rules.label: Methamphetamine/amphetamine + MDMA
rules.reason: Two stimulants together strain the heart and raise body temperature — risk of overheating and cardiac problems.

rules.label: Stimulants (cocaine, meth, amphetamine, MDMA) + MAOIs
rules.reason: Can cause a hypertensive crisis — a sudden, dangerous spike in blood pressure. Avoid entirely.

rules.label: Erection pills (Viagra/sildenafil, Cialis/tadalafil) + nitrates (poppers, nitroglycerin)
rules.reason: Both drop blood pressure; together they can cause a sudden, life-threatening collapse. Never combine — this includes recreational 'poppers'.

rules.label: Ketamine + opioids
rules.reason: Two sedating drugs — combined they deepen sedation and can suppress breathing, with a high risk of choking while unconscious.

rules.label: GHB + benzodiazepines
rules.reason: Two strong depressants — high risk of unconsciousness and stopped breathing.

rules.label: SSRIs + MAOIs
rules.reason: A classic, potentially fatal cause of serotonin syndrome. These are never combined without a supervised washout period between them.

rules.label: SSRIs/SNRIs (antidepressants) + tramadol
rules.reason: Raises the risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures. Only combine if a doctor has weighed it up.

rules.label: Alcohol + acetaminophen/paracetamol (Tylenol)
rules.reason: Both stress the liver; regular or heavy drinking with acetaminophen raises the risk of serious liver damage, even at normal doses.

rules.label: Alcohol + sleeping pills (zolpidem/Ambien, zopiclone)
rules.reason: Additive sedation that can suppress breathing, plus dangerous 'sleep-driving' and sleepwalking behaviours.

rules.label: Alcohol + sedating antihistamines (diphenhydramine/Benadryl)
rules.reason: Both cause drowsiness; together they impair coordination and alertness more than expected — don't drive.

rules.label: Alcohol + metronidazole/tinidazole (antibiotics)
rules.reason: Can cause a severe reaction — intense nausea, vomiting, flushing and racing heart. Avoid alcohol during, and for ~48-72h after, the course.

rules.label: Warfarin / blood thinners + NSAIDs (ibuprofen, aspirin, naproxen)
rules.reason: Adds bleeding risk on top of the blood thinner, especially stomach/gut bleeding.

rules.label: Warfarin + many antibiotics
rules.reason: Several antibiotics make warfarin thin the blood more, raising bleeding risk — extra monitoring is usually needed.

rules.label: Lithium + NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen)
rules.reason: NSAIDs push lithium levels toward toxic — dangerous because lithium's safe range is narrow.

rules.label: ACE inhibitors (lisinopril) + potassium supplements / salt substitutes
rules.reason: Both raise potassium; together they can push it to levels that disturb heart rhythm.

rules.label: Opioids + gabapentin/pregabalin
rules.reason: Gabapentinoids add to opioid sedation and breathing suppression — a recognised and rising overdose risk.

rules.label: Alcohol + insulin or sulfonylureas (gliclazide, glipizide)
rules.reason: Can cause dangerous low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia), sometimes hours later — eat when drinking and monitor.

rules.label: Cannabis + alcohol
rules.reason: Alcohol raises blood-THC levels; together they cause stronger dizziness, nausea and 'greening out', and heavily impair driving.

rules.label: Antipsychotics (olanzapine, quetiapine) + other depressants (alcohol, opioids, benzos)
rules.reason: Stacks sedation and can lower blood pressure and suppress breathing.
